A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAK-UCB/RFF-UCB research. The main text, algorithms, equations, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-selection experiments on image generation, code generation, and Sudoku, plus synthetic image-captioning and video experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The per-arm kernel regression, UCB selection and updates, RFF approximation, and theoretical algorithm variants remain unchanged in Algorithms 2–6.

E1.justification: Both retain MS-COCO image tasks, HumanEval/BigCodeBench code completion, HumanEval-X translation, Sudoku, and synthetic MSR-VTT video selection. The scenarios introducing new models and prompt categories are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain KernelUCB-poly3, One-arm Oracle, Random, PAK-UCB-lin, LinUCB, and Naive-KRR. The direct PAK-UCB-RBF versus RFF-UCB-RBF comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the same sampling, embeddings, model configurations, iteration budgets, and OtB/OPR metrics. This includes five responses per model to determine the OPR reference and the stated timing of model/prompt introductions.

E4.justification: Both retain adaptation experiments, generated-output examples, kernel and regularization sensitivity studies, RFF feature-count analyses, and approximation/runtime comparisons. No analysis is added or removed from Appendix C.

E5.justification: The reporting of averages over 20 trials, plotted error bars, and plus/minus values in model-score examples is unchanged. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical passages and Figures 1–32 retain the same scores, curves, rankings, and examples. Figure 32 still reports approximately 10 minutes for PAK-UCB-RBF versus under 2 minutes for RFF-UCB-RBF over 2,000 iterations.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, the regret theorems, complexity analysis, and proofs and auxiliary lemmas in Appendices A–B are retained. Differences in equation delimiters and placement are typesetting changes without revised mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about prompt-dependent rankings, online per-arm selection, regret guarantees, RFF computational savings, and empirical effectiveness. The revised title does not change their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of arm-specific selection and RFF efficiency, applicability to varying model rankings, and future directions concerning diversity and cost remain unchanged. The added Impact Statement supplies no substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: Both provide the same implementation information, including embeddings, D = 200, regularization alpha = 1, delta = 0.05, and code/model access links. Appendix C.4 adds no technical or reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against offline routing, shared-weight contextual bandits, and unconditional model selection remain unchanged. Bibliographic URLs, metadata, ordering, and duplicate-entry year suffixes change without adding research sources.

P1.justification: v5 revises the title to foreground PAK-UCB and prompt-aware selection, rewords the Section 4 heading, updates author/publication information, and adds Acknowledgements and an Impact Statement. Scientific prose and section organization remain essentially intact.

P2.justification: v5 comprehensively adopts conference formatting, with two-column main text and references, new typography and running headers, resized figures and algorithms, and redistributed appendix figures. All 32 figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–C retain the same methods, proofs, evidence, and reproducibility information. The revised title, conference layout, bibliographic metadata, and acknowledgement/impact sections are editorial changes with no meaningful net effect on the paper's scientific support or overall quality.
